newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares break 2,700 level for first time.
newsitem.headline: German shares break 2,700 level for first time.

text.p: German shares are expected to continue to advance next week, having broken the 2,700 level on Friday for the first time when Wall Street rallied on the back of weaker-than-expected U.S. jobless figures.

The IBIS DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares was up 17.92 points or 0.67 percent at 2703.21 in late afternoon electronic trade after hitting the record level of 2,703.59 after the early rise on the Dow Jones Industrial index.
U.S. September non-farm payrolls came in down 40,000, confounding market expectations of a rise of 166,000 and dampening expectations of a U.S. interest rate hike next month.
"The figures show no problems on the inflation side and thats very bond-positive at the moment," said a Frankfurt trader.
Dealers said there had been quite a lot of interest from American investors, adding that some dealers were even starting to talk about the DAX reaching the magical 3,000 point level.
"That we've reached a new high before a holiday and then we've gone further before the weekend is of course a very bullish sign," said one dealer.
Earlier on, stocks were supported by a strong dollar against the mark, which helped export-oriented German stocks.
Later in the day the dollar sank back and the IBIS DAX index had to looked elsewhere for inspiration, namely to Wall Street.
Volumes were light after many market players took a long weekend, following the Germany Unity Day holiday on Thursday. "Most people closed their books for the week on Wednesday," said one trader.
Dealers said the interim report of Allianz AG Holding on Monday would attract a lot of interest. Next Friday U.S. figures will be in the spotlight once more when producer prices data is released.

Building group Holzmann AG was the loss leader, tumbling 18 marks, over five percent, to 332 marks, after a Bild newspaper report said its chief executive could be sacked and replaced by the head of diversified industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG.
MG said the report was "nonsense" and Holzmann called the article "factually incorrect and speculative." Holzmann on Wednesday denied reports that the group had liquidity problems.
